business: Northstar, a self-hosted job-search and application workspace for Indian college students
by_segment: Final-year student preparing for campus placement
Pre-final-year student seeking a technical internship
why_not: I would check it out if it worked smoothly on my phone, but the self-hosting and setting up provider credentials sounds like friction I won't take on while juggling classes and placements.

I do lose track of rounds and follow-ups, so the idea is relevant, but I would not set up self-hosting and provider credentials just to try another tracker. I need something that works easily on my phone between classes, and that is not clear from this offer.

I would stick with the placement-cell and LinkedIn checks I already do; this sounds useful for organizing applications, but I don't know that it covers campus drives or enough relevant internship sources to change my routine.

I might use a tracker, but this sounds like another job board and I already keep applications in a spreadsheet. The project-based profile is relevant, though I need to know whether it actually covers campus drives and internships before I would switch.

I would try a free tracker, but I wouldn’t set up hosting or hand over paid search and AI credentials without knowing the internships are current, paid, and actually legitimate. I need the original posts and eligibility details before this saves me enough time to bother.

I would try the placement-cell and job-group links I already use before setting up a self-hosted workspace, especially when I can’t tell which postings are current or paid. I might reconsider if I could check the original listing quickly and verify it’s legitimate.

I would not pay for an AI job-search tool while I’m a student, and I can already use my coursework and projects to show what I can do. Since this concept is free but still needs my hosting and provider credentials, I’d rather keep using the tools I already have.

I already check placement messages, college groups, LinkedIn, seniors, and job boards, so I would keep using those before adding a self-hosted tool. Even though the software is free, hosting and provider credentials sound like extra cost and setup I don't want as a student.

I already check Internshala, Unstop, LinkedIn, and my placement cell, so I don't see a reason to add another place to search. Free is nice, but setting up hosting and provider credentials sounds like extra hassle while I'm applying.
why_yes: I’m actively preparing for placements, and keeping applications and rounds in one place would help. The project-based resume drafts sound useful if they stick to what I actually built.
